title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the opening page of the 'Notes sur l'équation fonctionnelle', and it records standard linear algebra. Grothendieck is preparing the formalism behind the Lefschetz-trace and functional-equation treatment of geometric L-functions.

1. Setup. Let f be an endomorphism of an n-dimensional vector space E over a field k. Define the reversed characteristic polynomial
 P_f(t) = det(1 - f t) = ∏_i (1 - λ_i t) = Σ_i (-1)^i Tr(Λ^i f) t^i,
where the λ_i are the eigenvalues in an algebraic closure of k. Its roots are the inverses of the nonzero eigenvalues of f.

2. Additivity. The assignment (E,f) ↦ P_f is 'additive': a short exact sequence of pairs (E,f) is sent to a product of polynomials. So P factors through K_0 of endomorphisms, landing in the multiplicative group 1 + t k[t].

3. Zeta function. Z_f(t) = 1/P_f(t) = ∏ 1/(1 - λ_i t) = Σ_ν t^ν h_ν(λ) = Σ_ν Tr(Sym^ν f) t^ν. This is the dual identity: complete symmetric functions versus elementary symmetric functions.

4. Tensor products. P sends tensor products of pairs (E,f) to a product * on power series with constant term 1. It is defined by (1 - a t) * (1 - b t) = 1 - a b t, extended by distributivity over ordinary multiplication. This is exactly the multiplication of the big Witt ring / the universal λ-ring Λ(k) = 1 + t k[[t]]. Hence P is a ring homomorphism from K_0(End_k) to Λ(k).

Purpose. In the geometric case, L-functions are alternating products of such P's for Frobenius acting on étale cohomology with compact support. Additivity gives multiplicativity in exact sequences, and the * product controls tensor products (Künneth, twisting) and duality. The functional equation should then come from Poincaré duality, which relates P for f on H^i to P for the transpose-inverse twisted by q^d on H^{2d-i}.

Margin sketch. The sketch in the lower right lists indices p-1, p, p+1, then -2, -1, 0, then p-1, p, p+1 and p-1, 0, p+1, joined by diagonal arrows. It looks like a degree-shift or pairing diagram for complexes, presumably for a duality/cone argument. It cannot be reliably interpreted.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page.
The term 'additif' is used in the sense 'turns direct sums/extensions into products'; this is consistent with the stated meaning.

ideas.what: Reversed characteristic polynomial det(1-ft) expressed via traces of exterior powers
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic polynomial / elementary symmetric functions of eigenvalues
ideas.where_published: SGA 4½ (Rapport sur la formule des traces), SGA 5, Bourbaki talk 279 (Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L, 1964)

ideas.modern_name: Generating function of complete symmetric polynomials; MacMahon master theorem type identity

ideas.what: P is multiplicative on exact sequences and sends tensor products to the product (1-at)*(1-bt)=1-abt
ideas.modern_name: Big Witt vectors / universal λ-ring Λ(A)=1+tA[[t]]; the characteristic-polynomial map as a ring homomorphism K_0(End) → W(k)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Witt and Cartier for Witt vectors; Grothendieck (1957–58) for the λ-ring structure on 1+tA[[t]]; Almkvist (1970s) for the theorem K_0(End) ≅ rational Witt vectors
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'La théorie des classes de Chern' (1958); SGA 6 Exposé V (Berthelot, on λ-ring structures)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard preliminaries: the characteristic polynomial, symmetric powers, and the Witt/λ-ring product, all well known and partly due to Grothendieck himself in his published λ-ring work. The margin sketch is uninterpretable.
transcription_corrections: The faint typed text visible on the page is show-through from a Bourbaki typescript on the reverse side, which is the same source as the 'next page' transcription (Haar measure, n°357). It is not part of these notes.
Line 2 of the formula should read Σ_i (-1)^i (Tr λ^i(f)) t^i, with λ^i denoting the exterior power; the transcription has this correctly.
